questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The ulcer has indurated edges, is clean-based, and non-tender on palpation. Dark-field microscopy of serous exudate reveals motile spirochetes. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU single IM dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose is the treatment of choice. Doxycycline is used in penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with SLE presents with a malar rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. Skin biopsy shows immunoglobulin deposition at the dermoepidermal junction on direct immunofluorescence. This finding is also known as:
questions.exp: The lupus band test (LBT) refers to the deposition of immunoglobulins (IgG, IgM, IgA) and complement at the dermoepidermal junction on direct immunofluorescence. It is positive in both lesional and non-lesional skin in SLE.

questions.q: A 40-year-old farmer from a leprosy-endemic area has a single hypopigmented anaesthetic patch on the trunk with a thickened peripheral nerve. Slit-skin smear is negative for AFB. Skin biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytes but no AFB. What is the classification of this leprosy?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) is characterized by a single or few well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, thickened nerves, negative smear, and skin biopsy showing well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytes but no AFB. CMI is high in TT.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lips, preceded by tingling/burning for 12 hours. The most likely causative organism and the mechanism of recurrence is:
opts: VZV; reactivation from dorsal root ganglia
questions.exp: Herpes labialis (cold sores) is caused by HSV-1. Primary infection establishes latency in the trigeminal ganglion, from which reactivation occurs due to triggers like UV exposure, stress, or fever.

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic patient develops a rapidly spreading necrotizing infection of the scrotum with severe pain, fever, and crepitus on examination. The most appropriate immediate management is:
opts: IV antibiotics alone for 72 hours before surgery
Emergency wide surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a type I (polymicrobial) necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum/genitalia, a surgical emergency. Immediate wide surgical debridement combined with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics is life-saving. Delay worsens mortality.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with tense vesicles and bullae on normal and erythematous skin, involving trunk and flexures, with intense pruritus. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. The antibody target is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterized by tense bullae, linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF, and autoantibodies targeting BP180 (BPAG2/type XVII collagen) and BP230. Desmoglein 3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris; collagen VII in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man has well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the scalp, elbows, and knees. Auspitz sign is positive. Histopathology reveals parakeratosis, elongation of rete ridges, thinning of suprapapillary plates, and neutrophilic microabscesses. These microabscesses are called:
questions.exp: In psoriasis, neutrophilic collections within the stratum corneum are called Munro microabscesses. Kogoj's spongiform pustules are neutrophilic collections within the spinous layer seen in pustular psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses are seen in mycosis fungoides.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man has a pearly white papule with telangiectasias and a rolled border on the nose, present for 2 years. Biopsy shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artefact. The best treatment with lowest recurrence rate is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) with pearly rolled border and telangiectasias is the most common skin cancer. Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rate (99%) with tissue sparing, especially for high-risk/recurrent/facial BCC.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman from South India develops confluent hyperpigmented macules on the cheeks and forehead, worsening in summer. She is on oral contraceptive pills. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation. The most likely diagnosis and first-line treatment is:
opts: Melasma; sun protection with topical triple combination cream
questions.exp: Melasma is a common acquired hypermelanosis triggered by sun exposure, oral contraceptives, and pregnancy. Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal melasma. First-line treatment is strict sun protection plus triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + mild steroid).

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive man on HAART develops multiple painless ulcers in the mouth and brown-red papules on the trunk and extremities. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells with vascular spaces and RBCs extravasating into tissue, with HHV-8 positive cells. Diagnosis and treatment of choice:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in HIV is caused by HHV-8. Classic presentation: violaceous plaques/papules on extremities and mucosa. For disseminated or rapidly progressive KS, liposomal doxorubicin (pegylated) is first-line systemic therapy. HAART optimization also critical.

questions.q: A 28-year-old patient with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and pathergy test positivity. The condition is associated with HLA-B51. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behçet's disease is a systemic vasculitis characterized by the classic triad of recurrent oral aphthae, genital ulcers, and uveitis, along with positive pathergy test. It is strongly associated with HLA-B51, particularly in patients from the Silk Road region.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child develops honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth, spreading rapidly over 3 days. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The causative organism and mechanism of bulla formation in bullous impetigo is:
opts: S. aureus phage type 71; exfoliative toxin A/B cleaving desmoglein 1
S. aureus; protein A blocking IgG
questions.exp: Bullous impetigo is caused by S. aureus (phage group II, type 71) producing exfoliative toxins A and B, which are serine proteases that specifically cleave desmoglein 1 in the superficial epidermis, causing subcorneal blisters.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the right T5 dermatome, preceded by 3 days of burning pain. The risk of which complication is significantly reduced by early antiviral treatment within 72 hours?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (reactivation of VZV) causes dermatomal vesicular eruption. Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is the most common complication (pain persisting >3 months). Early antiviral treatment (acyclovir/valacyclovir/famciclovir) within 72 hours of rash onset significantly reduces PHN risk.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with multiple ring-shaped scaly patches on the trunk, with central clearing and active raised border. KOH mount shows hyphae. The drug of choice for extensive tinea corporis is:
questions.exp: Extensive tinea corporis requires systemic antifungal therapy. Oral terbinafine 250mg daily for 2-4 weeks is preferred due to its fungicidal action against dermatophytes, better efficacy, shorter duration, and fewer drug interactions compared to griseofulvin.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with flaccid bullae in the mouth and skin that rupture easily, leaving raw erosions. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition in a 'chicken-wire' pattern. The antigen targeted is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris involves mucosal and skin lesions, flaccid bullae, positive Nikolsky sign, and DIF showing intercellular IgG in a chicken-wire/fishnet pattern. Antibodies target Desmoglein 3 (mucosae) and Desmoglein 1 (skin) — Dsg3 is primary in mucosal-dominant disease.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man from Bihar presents with painless nodular swelling of both earlobes, diffuse thickening of facial skin (leonine facies), madarosis, and a positive slit-skin smear showing Globi on AFB staining. The Ridley-Jopling classification is:
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) features multiple lesions, leonine facies, madarosis, ear lobe thickening, and high bacterial load (Globi on smear). CMI is poor/absent, allowing uncontrolled multiplication of M. leprae.

questions.q: A 19-year-old man has multiple comedones, inflammatory papules, and pustules on the face, chest, and back. He has not responded to topical benzoyl peroxide and clindamycin for 3 months. The next best step in management is:
questions.exp: Moderate-to-severe acne refractory to topical therapy warrants oral isotretinoin (0.5–1 mg/kg/day). It addresses all pathogenic factors (sebum production, comedogenesis, P. acnes, inflammation). Pregnancy prevention is mandatory due to teratogenicity.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with scaling, erythema, and fissuring of the finger webs and palmar surfaces, worsening on contact with water and detergents. Patch testing is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Irritant contact dermatitis (ICD) is caused by direct physical/chemical damage without immunological sensitization. Wet work and detergents are classic triggers. Patch testing is negative (distinguishing it from allergic contact dermatitis, where patch testing is positive).

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with progressive tightening of facial skin, Raynaud's phenomenon, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Nailfold capillaroscopy shows dilated capillary loops. ANA shows centromere pattern. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is the limited cutaneous form of SSc. Anti-centromere antibody is characteristic. Nailfold capillaroscopy showing dilated loops supports the diagnosis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a 2 cm ulcerated nodule on the lower lip with indurated margins, present for 6 months. Biopsy shows islands of atypical squamous cells with keratin pearl formation invading the dermis. The most important prognostic factor for metastasis is:
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip carries a 10-15% metastasis risk. Perineural invasion is the single most important histological predictor of recurrence and metastasis in cutaneous SCC. Other high-risk features include depth >2mm, poor differentiation, and immunosuppression.

questions.q: In the treatment of onychomycosis due to T. rubrum, oral terbinafine is given as a continuous course. The recommended duration for toenail involvement is:
questions.exp: For toenail onychomycosis, oral terbinafine 250mg/day is given for 12 weeks (continuous) — the nail plate continues to improve for months after stopping treatment. For fingernails, 6 weeks is usually sufficient. Pulse itraconazole is an alternative.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with target lesions (concentric rings) on the palms, soles, and oral mucosa following a course of sulfonamides for a UTI. Skin biopsy shows interface dermatitis with necrotic keratinocytes. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) involves target lesions, mucosal involvement of ≥2 sites, epidermal detachment <10% BSA, caused by drugs (sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol). Histology: interface dermatitis with full-thickness epidermal necrosis and necrotic keratinocytes.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with patchy hair loss with exclamation mark hairs at the periphery. Dermoscopy shows yellow dots, black dots, and broken hairs. Pull test is positive. The most appropriate first-line treatment for localized alopecia areata is:
questions.exp: Intralesional corticosteroid injection (triamcinolone acetonide 5-10mg/mL) is the first-line treatment for localized (patchy) alopecia areata, producing the best short-term hair regrowth. Exclamation mark hairs and positive pull test confirm active AA.

questions.q: During a skin biopsy, the dermoscope reveals a dark lesion with an asymmetric multicomponent pattern. Biopsy shows junctional activity, pagetoid spread, and irregular nesting of atypical melanocytes. The Clark level describes invasion into which layer?
questions.exp: Clark's levels describe melanoma depth: I=epidermis only; II=papillary dermis; III=fills papillary dermis (papillary-reticular interface); IV=invades reticular dermis; V=subcutaneous fat. Clark IV indicates deep reticular dermal invasion with higher metastatic potential.

questions.q: A patient with pustular psoriasis in pregnancy develops fever, generalized pustules, and hypocalcaemia. The safest systemic treatment in this scenario is:
questions.exp: Impetigo herpetiformis (pustular psoriasis of pregnancy) is severe. Methotrexate and acitretin are teratogenic (Category X). Cyclosporine is considered the safest systemic option in pregnancy for severe psoriasis when systemic treatment is necessary.

questions.q: A 27-year-old man presents with painless penile ulcer that healed spontaneously, followed 6 weeks later by a generalized skin rash involving palms and soles, with non-tender lymphadenopathy. VDRL is reactive 1:64. The stage and preferred treatment is:
opts: Primary syphilis; benzathine penicillin 2.4MU IM single dose
Secondary syphilis; benzathine penicillin 2.4MU IM single dose
Secondary syphilis; benzathine penicillin 7.2MU total (3 doses weekly)
Latent syphilis; benzathine penicillin 7.2MU IM (3 doses weekly)
questions.exp: The healed chancre followed by generalized rash (including palms/soles), lymphadenopathy, and reactive VDRL 1:64 represents secondary syphilis (within 2 years). Treatment: benzathine penicillin G 2.4MU IM single dose. Three-dose regimen is for late latent or unknown duration.

questions.q: Langerhans cells in the epidermis are derived from which precursors and are identified by which marker on electron microscopy?
opts: Bone marrow monocyte precursors; Birbeck granules
questions.exp: Langerhans cells (antigen-presenting cells of the epidermis) are bone marrow-derived (monocyte/macrophage lineage) and characterized by unique tennis-racquet shaped Birbeck granules on electron microscopy. They express CD1a and Langerin (CD207).

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with hypopigmented macules on the upper trunk, shoulders and back, associated with fine scaling. KOH preparation reveals short curved hyphae and spherical yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs' appearance). The most effective treatment for extensive lesions is:
opts: Topical selenium sulphide shampoo 2.5% weekly for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur) showing 'spaghetti and meatballs' on KOH. For extensive disease, oral itraconazole 200mg/day for 5-7 days is highly effective. Ketoconazole is also used but has more hepatotoxicity concerns. Topicals work for limited disease.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops progressive purple-red discolouration of the eyelids (heliotrope rash), Gottron's papules over the knuckles, and proximal muscle weakness. CK is elevated. The most important investigation to evaluate internal malignancy is:
opts: CT scan of chest, abdomen and pelvis
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults has 15-25% association with underlying malignancy (ovarian, lung, GI, breast). CT scan of chest, abdomen and pelvis is the most important investigation to screen for occult malignancy. Anti-Jo-1 is associated with antisynthetase syndrome (ILD, not malignancy).

questions.q: A patient presents with a well-defined erythematous plaque at the same site on the lip, recurring with each course of sulfamethoxazole. The lesion heals with hyperpigmentation. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Fixed drug eruption (FDE) characteristically recurs at the same site with each re-exposure to the offending drug (common culprits: sulfonamides, NSAIDs, tetracyclines). Heals with residual hyperpigmentation. Histology shows interface dermatitis with melanophages.

questions.q: In a patient undergoing treatment for multi-bacillary leprosy (MB-MDT), sudden appearance of multiple new erythematous nodular lesions with fever, malaise and nerve tenderness occurs. FNAC of the lesion shows foamy macrophages laden with AFB. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL and LL leprosy during treatment, presenting with painful nodular erythematous lesions, fever, neuritis, and systemic symptoms. Histology shows foamy macrophages with high AFB load. Type 1 (reversal) occurs in borderline spectrum with upgrading CMI.
